newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-West power mostly steady in mild weather.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-West power mostly steady in mild weather.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West were mostly steady amidst continued mild weather, industry sources said.
"It doesn't look like we are going to see much change this week with the weather holding at these cool levels," one trader said.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), on peak electricity for a 16-hour block for delivery Friday was talked steady in the $15.00-17.00 range, with off-peak power in the region pegged slightly lower at $8.00-$8.50 from discussion near $8.50 on Wednesday.

On-peak prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Friday delivery were said to be discussed slightly higher at $15.50-17.50 from a Wednesday range of $15.00-17.00, with off-peak power pegged near $11.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.
The MAIN prices were said to have risen slightly due to some line loading out of the MAPP region, the sources said.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Friday delivery were also quoted steady in the $14.00-16.00 range, the sources said.
Longer-term ECAR peak power prices also held steady, with the remainder of September discussed near $15.50 and October at close to $17.00.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Thursday delivery was assessed in the $16.00-16.50 range in the southern area of the region, with off-peak power pegged steady in the $14.00-15.00 range.
In the northern area of SPP, power was assessed steady in the $13.00-14.00 range, with off-peak electricity discussed in the 10.50-12.50 range, the brokers and marketers said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
